sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Entry 90 MANAMBU, p.27: 'Villages: Avatip, Malu, Yambon, Yau'umbak [CD 45E], Sengo? [CD 42E].. The SIL team of R. and M. Farnsworth.. state (personal communication) that the village of Sengo is reported to speak the same language, but are not sure. Otherwise, Sengo will speak a Sepik Plains dialect.' Identity/village note only; nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1965. The Ndu language family (Sepik District, New Guinea). Pacific Linguistics C-1. Canberra: ANU. 236 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sengo is never mentioned (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing). Sec. 5.2 Stress pp.29-30 is for Wosera Abelam only (non-phonemic, nucleus-rank rule); ch.11 Manambu (pp.120-121) and ch.10 Iatmul (pp.113-114) give no stress-placement rule; ch.14 'Notes on the Sawos language' pp.143-144: no material elicited. The earlier scan's pointer to this work is family-level only.

sources.citation: Jendraschek, Gerd. 2012. A grammar of Iatmul. Habilitationsschrift, Universität Regensburg.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: pp.4-8 treat the 'Sawos' varieties and the Iatmul dialect continuum into which Aikhenvald 2008 places Sengo; pp.91-93 give the Iatmul stress rule (per Wikipedia summary: long vowel > CVC > initial). If Sengo is an Iatmul dialect this is the nearest full description.

sources.note: The only reference Glottolog tags for Sengo [spk] (Glottolog's most extensive description 'wordlist or less'); a lexicostatistic overview with wordlists of Sengo, Burui, Gaikundi, Sos Kundi, Koiwat and Iatmul dialects. May carry stress marks in its transcriptions and settles Sengo's placement (Iatmul vs Manambu); a prose stress rule is unlikely.
